title: Entity Adapter
description: Learn how to use createEntityAdapter for automated normalized state management in Redux Toolkit.

data.text: Manually normalizing state and writing all the update logic can become repetitive. Every time you add a new entity type, you write similar code for adding, updating, and deleting items. **Redux Toolkit's `createEntityAdapter`** solves this by generating all that boilerplate automatically.

An entity adapter provides pre-built reducers for common CRUD operations and memoized selectors for efficient data retrieval. Instead of writing normalization logic from scratch, you configure an adapter once and get everything you need.

data.text: Entity adapters provide a complete set of methods for managing normalized state. These methods handle the immutability updates automatically, so you don't have to worry about spreading objects correctly.

data.caption: Entity adapter operations flow
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A["API Response
(entity array)"] --> B[addMany]
    B --> C["Normalized State
{ byId: {...}, ids: [...] }"]
    C --> D[getSelectors]
    D --> E[selectAll / selectById]
    C --> F[updateOne]
    F --> C
    C --> G[removeOne]
    G --> C

data.text: Along with reducers, entity adapters generate memoized selectors. These selectors are optimized to only recompute when the relevant data actually changes, preventing unnecessary re-renders in your components.

data.title: Generated Selectors

data.text: The `updateOne` method uses an object with an `id` and `changes` property. This lets you update specific fields without replacing the entire entity. The changes object is shallowly merged with the existing entity.

data.title: Consistent Patterns
data.text: Using entity adapters across your application creates a consistent pattern for handling all entity data, making your codebase easier to understand and maintain.
